06.09.2025 REFERENCE PETITION UNDER SECTION 18 OF THE LAND ACQUISITION ACT 1894 AWARD:
(BY THE COURT U/S 26 OF LAND ACQUISITION ACT- 1894 ON REFERENCE PETITION U/S 18 OF THE ACT):
1. Vide this judgment I shall decide the reference u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter called as LA Act), filed by the petitioner for enhancement in compensation of the land as mentioned in reference u/s 18 LA Act, situated in the revenue estate of village Iradat Nagar @ Naya Bans, Delhi.
2.

Brief facts of the case are that large tract of Land measuring 214 bigha 10 biswa of village Iradat Nagar@ Naya Bans, Delhi, was acquired by the Govt. for a public purpose namely "Development of Freight Complex Narela under planned development of Delhi".

Notification under Section 4 of The Land Acquisition Act,
1894 was issued on SIDHARTH MATHUR MATHUR Date:
2025.09.06 12:32:51 +0530 22.08.2001; Declaration under Section 6 of LA Act was made on 26.07.2002.

Thereafter, Award bearing no.
07/DC/NW/ 2004-05 was announced by Land Acquisition Collector (hereinafter referred to as LAC) on 15.06.2004.
The LAC determined the market price of the acquired land as Rs. 15.70 lac per acre for category A Land and Rs. 14 lacs for Category B Land.
3. The petitioner, being dissatisfied with the market value determined by the LAC, filed the present petition u/s 18 of the LA Act, seeking reference to this court.
The LAC forwarded the same to this Court for adjudication.

4. The case of the petitioners is that they were the bhumidars/absolute owners as well as in cultivatory possession of the land bearing khasra numbers as mentioned in the Statement u/s 19 of the LA Act that was annexed with the present reference and admitted by the petitioner during the stage of admission/denial of documents, situated within the Revenue Estate of Village Iradat Nagar @ Naya Bans Delhi (the said land).

The said land was acquired vide notification dated 22.08.2001.
5.
The petitioner has challenged the said award inter alia on the ground of inadequacy of compensation and incorrect SIDHARTH MATHUR MATHUR

Date:
2025.09.06 12:32:57 +0530 assessment of market value of land inter-alia due to non- consideration of relevant factors like potentiality and fertility of the suit land, the surrounding colonies and developed areas, the market value of the adjoining areas/villages, the sale deeds of other lands of the contemporary period, nearness to Jag Dev Singh vs Union Of India ( 7/04-05 Nayaj Bans ... on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178554010/
2 the National Highway and industrial areas, the amenities available in the suit land etc.
6. The petitioner has prayed compensation at enhanced rate besides interest thereon and solatium in addition to the compensation.
7.

sentences.text: The respondent no.1 (UOI)/Land Acquisition Collector has failed to file its WS within stipulated time.
Hence, his right to file WS was closed vide order dt. 22.10.2024 and respondent no.2/Delhi Development Authority (DDA)
contested the reference petition by filing its Written Statement.

8. The petition has been contested mainly on the ground that the LAC awarded adequate compensation to the petitioner after taking into consideration all the relevant factors and therefore,
LAC has correctly assessed the market value of the land after taking into account the market rates prevailing at the time of notification under Section 4 of LA SIDHARTH by SIDHARTH MATHUR MATHUR Date: 2025.09.06 12:33:04 +0530 Act.
9.
During the stage of admission-denial of documents, the counsel for petitioner admitted the statement given u/s 19 of the Act.

The following issues were framed :-
i) Whether the petitioner is entitled to enhancement in compensation, if so, to what amount?
ii) Relief.
10.
In evidence, the counsel for petitioner on behalf of petitioner has relied upon the judgment in a case Jai Singh vs. UOI LAA 266/2008 D.O.D 23.08.2011 and has led the evidence in the said case.

11. The respondent no.1/Union of India/UOI in its evidence, tendered the award as Ex. R-1 and respondent no.2/Delhi Development Authority adopted the evidence led on behalf of respondent no.1/UOI.
12.
I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have also carefully considered the record.
My issue-wise findings are given as under:-
SIDHARTH
Petitioner has contended that valuation of land determined by LAC is not reasonable as LAC has not adopted the correct method of valuation.
However, he has not led any evidence to show as to how the LAC was wrong in fixing market value of land.

Ld. Counsel for the petitioner has also relied upon the judgment titled as Rajpal Vs. UOI in LAC No. 81A/08 decided by Ld. Predecessor Sh.

sentences.text:
Ld. Counsel for the petitioner argued that Rajpal Vs. UOI(Supra)
pertained to the same village, same notifications and same award by which the land of the present petitioner is acquired.
Hence, same market value of petitioner's land be determined.
14. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for the respondent has not led any evidence only tendered the copy of the award.
15. In Rajpal Vs. UOI (Supra), Ld. Predecessor had determined the market value @ Rs.16,74,500 per acre for Category A Land and Rs.16,32,640/- for Category B Land.
16. Since, no evidence has been led by respondents to controvert the said judgment, therefore, I find no justification to differ from the judgment in Rajpal Vs. UOI (supra).
Hence, I determine the same market value.

17. Besides above, petitioner shall be entitled to other SIDHARTH MATHUR MATHUR Date:
2025.09.06 12:33:14 +0530 statutory benefit i.e 12% Addl. Amount as per section 23 (1) A & 30% solatium u/s 23 (2) & will be entitled to interest on the market value @
9% per annum for the first year & 15% for subsequent year till the making of payment of enhanced compensation by LAC as per provision of Section 28 of the Act.
Issue no.1 decided accordingly.
18. Findings on Issue No.2 - RELIEF

Date:
2025.09.06 12:33:19 +0530 annum on the difference between the enhanced compensation awarded by this court and the compensation awarded by the LAC for the subsequent period till its payment.
It was ordered that LRs of petitioner no.2 shall not entitled to interest for the period w.e.f. 01.06.2023 till 18.01.2024.
